VELORA — brand asset

Monogram

A strip of card, folded once, read as the letter V. The fold is carried by tone rather than by a drawn line, so the mark holds at every size and collapses cleanly into a single-colour V.

On the dark surface

Two tones, and one

Two tones — the default. The turned-away plane is held at 0.74.

One tone — foiling, embroidery, one-colour print, and anywhere a second tone is unavailable.

Construction

A 32×32 grid. Seven points, one crease, no feature below 1 unit — nothing depends on a fine detail to stay recognisable.

  • Cut ends 4.16, 7.21 → 9.04, 4.67, perpendicular to the strip
  • Crease x = 16, from the notch 18 to the foot 27.34
  • Foot 14.67 → 17.33 — the folded edge seen edge-on
  • Minimum size 16px on screen, 12mm in print
  • Clear space 12 units on every side

Wordmark

Outlines, not live text: converted from the shipped Cormorant Garamond subset at weight 400, letterspaced. A wordmark set as live text changes with whatever font the viewer happens to have, reflows when a webfont fails to load, and cannot be handed to a printer.

Clear space and lockup

Half the mark's width on every side. The hatched ring is the exclusion zone.

The lockup: outlines converted from the shipped Cormorant Garamond subset, set beside the mark with 20 units of clear space. No live text, no font dependency — this file can go to a printer or an embroiderer as it stands.

Type specimen

The brief makes Aref Ruqaa "subject to legibility testing". This is that test, on the real subsets: the abjad at reading size, then the same faces at the sizes the interface will use. Arabic must join; a subset that loses a shaping feature shows open, disconnected letters.
